terms.what: The game's name and logo word (package push_up_bird). "Beak" + "bound": a bird bound for somewhere, on its way with the mail.
where: UI: Level Builder share line and import errors
terms.guidance: The brand stays in Latin letters in EVERY language, including ja, ko, zh-Hant, ru and ar; never translate or transliterate it. In Arabic, isolate it as a left-to-right run inside right-to-left text; keep the all-caps BEAKBOUND logo form where the UI uses it.
terms.example: Update Beakbound to sync

terms.what: The fixed prefix of a Level Builder share code (BEAK1. followed by encoded data). Pasting a code finds it by this prefix.
where: UI: Level Builder (share code, paste code, import errors)
terms.guidance: Technical token: never translate, transliterate or change case; keep the dot. Only the sentence around it is translated ("Copy a friend's level code (it starts with BEAK1.) and tap Paste code again.").

terms.what: One of the four courier birds the player flies: a small, earnest, studious rookie who counts everything, makes notes and quotes Bill's rules; high, slightly squeaky voice (ElevenLabs: Nelson – Awkward Nerd Character). Leaves "Sunshine bubbles" behind him. Tagline "Small bird. Big sky."
where: flight voice (271 own lines + 4 sprint calls)
terms.guidance: Personal name: keep the spelling in Latin-script languages (es-419, pt-BR, id, fr, de, tr); transliterate phonetically in ja/ko/zh-Hant/ru/ar (ja katakana, ko hangul, zh-Hant phonetic characters, ru Cyrillic, ar Arabic script) and use that one spelling everywhere. Pronounced /pɪp/ (a "pip" is a tiny seed; the meaning is never used in a joke). Grammatical gender: masculine recommended (owner to confirm). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Rookie courier Pip, reporting for duty! Ahem. Flying now.

terms.what: One of the four courier birds: a pink bird with rosy cheeks and a curly crest, sweet, bubbly and affectionate, who gives everyone pet names and hugs (ElevenLabs: Cherry Twinkle – Adorable Cartoon Girl). Leaves "Peach hearts" behind her. Tagline "Rosy cheeks, curly crest, all heart."
where: flight voice (271 own lines + 4 sprint calls)
terms.guidance: Personal name: keep the spelling in Latin-script languages (es-419, pt-BR, id, fr, de, tr); transliterate phonetically in ja/ko/zh-Hant/ru/ar (ja katakana, ko hangul, zh-Hant phonetic characters, ru Cyrillic, ar Arabic script) and use that one spelling everywhere. The name means the fruit (peach-pink feathers); a few of her own lines pun on it ("Toasted peach!", "Salty peach smoothie!"): adapt those puns to the fruit word of your language while the name itself stays Peaches. Grammatical gender: feminine recommended (owner to confirm). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Magnet on! Come to Peaches, little stars!

terms.what: One of the four courier birds and the DEFAULT FIRST BIRD a new player flies: a tiny mint-green hummingbird, cheerful, quick, cocky and speed-mad, always racing and bragging (ElevenLabs: Teddy Twinkle – Cute Cartoon Boy). Leaves "Mint leaves" behind him. Tagline "Tiny hummer. Fresh sprig. Full speed."
where: flight voice (271 own lines + 4 sprint calls)
UI: settings reset ("Minty is ready for you")
terms.guidance: Personal name: keep the spelling in Latin-script languages (es-419, pt-BR, id, fr, de, tr); transliterate phonetically in ja/ko/zh-Hant/ru/ar (ja katakana, ko hangul, zh-Hant phonetic characters, ru Cyrillic, ar Arabic script) and use that one spelling everywhere. The name means "of mint" (his colour); it ties into the Spitter King's brew turning "minty" and Minty's "Try mint tea. Named after me, basically." Keep the name; adapt that joke to your word for mint. Grammatical gender: masculine recommended (owner to confirm). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Minty express!

terms.what: One of the four courier birds: a dreamy, sleepy, gentle little owl who flies by starlight and talks in soft images of moon, stars and bedtime (ElevenLabs: Lola – Soft, Innocent and Calming). Leaves "Stardust sparkles" behind her. Tagline "A dreamy owl who flies by starlight."
where: flight voice (271 own lines + 4 sprint calls)
terms.guidance: Personal name: keep the spelling in Latin-script languages (es-419, pt-BR, id, fr, de, tr); transliterate phonetically in ja/ko/zh-Hant/ru/ar (ja katakana, ko hangul, zh-Hant phonetic characters, ru Cyrillic, ar Arabic script) and use that one spelling everywhere. The name is the word "orbit" (moons and stars; "I'm a little moon now, pulling stars close"); keep it as a name, do not translate it. Grammatical gender: feminine recommended (owner to confirm).
terms.example: Hello, sky. It's me again, the owl with the letters.

terms.what: The old pelican who runs the Sky Club post: the courier's warm, eccentric mentor who briefs every route, gives the fight tips and tells bad jokes. His bill pouch was the club's first mailbag. Voice: GERALD – Exciting Older Voice (warm, colourful old British). Name tag on all his story lines.
where: flight voice (the birds quote "Bill says…", "Bill's tip")
terms.guidance: Bill is a personal name: keep/transliterate it (see the bird names). "Postmaster" is a title: translate it with title.postmaster and order it as your language does (title before or after the name). English pun: a pelican has a big BILL (beak), and a "bill" is also a piece of paper mail; it cannot survive translation and need not. Grammatical gender: masculine. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: There you are, rookie! Postmaster Bill. Welcome to the Sky Club post.

terms.what: The player's bird in its job: the Sky Club's newest mail courier. In story scenes the courier's line is ONE caption shared by all four birds (recorded in each bird's voice); bosses address it as "courier".
where: data: boss lines ("little courier", "This route has a courier.")
terms.guidance: Pick ONE word for "courier" (mail carrier / messenger who flies the post) and use it everywhere: story, flight lines, postcards, Neferhoo's "Royal Courier" and Pip's "Courier Pip". Its gender must work for all four birds: prefer an epicene noun or your language's accepted generic form, and phrase the shared story captions gender-neutrally (see CHARACTERS.md). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Sky Club post! I have a letter for you, sir.

terms.what: The unseen storybook narrator who reads the place captions: the prologue's opening plate and the "To be continued…" card. No name tag. Voice: Twinkle – Narration & Acting (gentle storybook).
terms.guidance: Never named on screen; only the role is given here. Write the captions as a calm storybook voice addressing the player directly ("Your first day."), gender-neutral.
terms.example: The Sky Club post. Sunrise. Your first day.

terms.what: Chapter 1 boss (lair 1-8, the Aztec temple top): a smug, posh aristocrat bat with a crown who took the Canopy Route because the morning post wakes him at sunrise; he wants his beauty sleep. Ends with the canopy delivered at dusk. Voice: Posh Josh. Masculine.
where: data: level 1-8 name, cargo 1-8, thank-you signer
terms.guidance: Descriptive title + species: translate naturally ("Baron" as a noble rank + your word for bat) and keep the B-B alliteration if it comes easily. Use one form everywhere; short forms are "the Baron" and the address "Baron". He is also "Lord of the Storm" on his card. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Baron Bat, at your disservice.

terms.what: Chapter 2 boss (lair 2-9, Ancient Arabia): a beetle king and excitable mad alchemist with a flask for a crown, who boils letters to brew an ink that never fades. Ends as the club's ink-maker, his brew turned to mint tea. Voice: Dr. Von Fusion – VF. Masculine.
where: data: level 2-9 name, cargo 2-9, thank-you signer
UI: vanguard banner ("THE SPITTER KING'S BROOD")
terms.guidance: "Spitter" = one who spits: he is the king of the spitter beetles (enemy.spitter-beetle), so reuse the SAME "spitter" word as that enemy. The card and data write "Spitter King" with no article; in sentences "the Spitter King"; Bill calls him "King"; birds say "Your Majesty". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The Spitter King! Bill's orders: don't drink anything!

terms.what: Chapter 3 boss (lair 3-8, Paris): a giant, velvety dusk-moth empress with a diadem who speaks in a hush. Her moths kept bumping into the lamps, so she put the city lamps to bed; she ends lighting them herself each dusk, with lampshades. Voice: Enchantress. Feminine.
where: data: level 3-8 name, cargo 3-8, thank-you signer
UI: vanguard banner ("THE DUSK EMPRESS'S MOTHS")
terms.guidance: Translate as a title: the "dusk" word must match enemy.dusk-moth (she is their empress). Short forms "the Empress" / address "Empress"; Pip once calls her "Her Highness". Feminine. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Shh. You will wake the lamps.

terms.what: Chapter 4 boss (lair 4-8, Open Sea): a gruff West Country sea dog on a ship with a cannon and a parrot, who raids mailbags for the STAMPS, not the letters (a stamp collector). Ends with the club sending him a stamp from every route. Voice: Matthew Schmitz – Old Pirate Captain. Masculine.
where: data: level 4-8 name, cargo 4-8 ("the Captain"), thank-you signer
terms.guidance: Translate naturally ("pirate captain" in your language). Short form "the Captain" / address "Captain"; he refers to himself as "the Captain" ("This be the Captain's water"). His speech is stage-pirate dialect: adapt it to your language's pirate idiom (see CHARACTERS.md). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Ahoy! What's in the bag, postie? Stamps, I hope!

terms.what: Chapter 5 final boss (lair 5-8, China, at the Edge of the Map): an ancient, grand, weary and lonely dragon who sent the four flame-seal letters because nobody ever wrote to him. The last delivery is the first letter ever addressed to him; he becomes the keeper of the beacon on route six. Voice: Smoke – The Dragon. Masculine.
where: data: level 5-8 name, cargo 5-8 ("the Dragon"), thank-you signer
terms.guidance: "Ember" = a glowing coal (fire that is old and quiet but still bites: "Embers remember how to bite."). Translate as a title. Short form "the Dragon" / address "Dragon"; the letter reads "Dear Dragon" and is addressed "The Ember Dragon, Edge of the Map". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Your wings are paper, little spark. I am the fire.

terms.what: Egypt's guardian (2-6, Return to Sender): the Mummy Courier, a 4,000-year-old hoopoe wrapped in linen in the golden mask of the Pharaoh's post, the Sky Club's first Egypt courier; fussy, proper, quick to take offence, warm and silly underneath. His one undelivered letter (for the Sphinx) is the club's lost letter. Voice: Herbie (Old Man with a Lisp and whistle S sounds). Masculine.
terms.guidance: Personal name: keep the spelling in Latin-script languages (es-419, pt-BR, id, fr, de, tr); transliterate phonetically in ja/ko/zh-Hant/ru/ar (ja katakana, ko hangul, zh-Hant phonetic characters, ru Cyrillic, ar Arabic script) and use that one spelling everywhere. Say it NEF-er-hoo (/ˈnɛfərhuː/): "Nefer" sounds ancient Egyptian (as in Nefertiti), "hoo" from hoopoe. Peaches calls him "Mister Neferhoo"; Orbit "old courier". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Neferhoo, Royal Courier. Four thousand years on this route.

terms.what: New York's first guardian (3-2, Wheels in the Rain): a huge, plump, grumpy pouter pigeon in a police cap, Commissioner of the Curb, who closes the sky because someone moved his bread cart; he blusters, sulks and deflates. Ends as Commissioner of the club's pigeonholes for a hot bagel a day. Voice: to audition (fallback Rusty Malone – Deep & Raspy); his story clips are pending recording, the captions show. Masculine.
where: UI: guardian name card (and the "COO!" shout)
terms.guidance: A pun: "Coo" is the sound a pigeon makes (and "King Coo" echoes King Kong, New York's famous giant). Recreate it as "King" + your language's pigeon-cooing sound, or keep "King Coo" if that sound reads as cooing in your language; keep it short (card title) and identical on the card, map, banner and unlock note. He calls himself "the Commissioner" in the third person.
terms.example: Nobody flies till the bread cart is found!

terms.what: New York's second guardian (3-4, Storm Warning): a limestone eagle gargoyle bolted to the tallest tower in 1931 with two searchlights for eyes and a lamp in his chest; a theatrical old ham who calls everyone "darling" and is lonely because "nobody looks up". Ends as the night mail's landing light. Bill nicknames him "Stoneface". Voice: to audition (fallback Eldrin); story clips pending recording. Masculine.
where: UI: guardian name card (two lines: "THE SEARCHLIGHT" / "GARGOYLE")
Play Games achievement "Out of the Spotlight"
terms.guidance: Translate as a descriptive name (your word for a searchlight + gargoyle, the stone figure on old buildings). The card splits it over two lines, small "THE SEARCHLIGHT" over big "GARGOYLE": choose a form that splits the same way or tell the UI translator. Short form "the Gargoyle", which he also uses for himself ("The Gargoyle accepts."). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: A visitor! Step into the light, darling, let me look at you!

terms.what: Two young toucan twins in the jungle whose birthday card is the courier's very first delivery; the postcard's "the toucans say thank you (very loudly)" is them and their family. Voice of the thank-you: Minnie – high pitch cartoon character.
where: UI: level 1-1 result (thank-you signer "The toucan twins")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The toucan twins") and voices it. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

terms.what: A choir of penguins in Antarctica who get woolly hats. Voice of the thank-you: Lulu Lollipop – Sweet & Bubbly Girl.

terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The penguin choir") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. Plural, happy ("Warm heads, high notes."). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

terms.what: The staff of an Antarctic research station who get hot cocoa. Voice of the thank-you: celine – cuddly, thin and soft..
where: UI: level 5-2 result (thank-you signer "The polar station")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The polar station") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. A place speaking for its crew; soft and relieved. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

terms.what: The chef of a neon noodle bar in Cyberpunk City whose sign needs spare fuses. Voice of the thank-you: DEVILL – English Speaking Korean Male Streamer.
where: UI: level 5-3 result (thank-you signer "The noodle chef")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The noodle chef") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. Singular, masculine, excited ("OPEN again" quotes the sign). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.

terms.what: Racers who run across the rooftops of Cyberpunk City and get race tickets. Voice of the thank-you: Gigi – Cute, Peppy, Energetic.
where: UI: level 5-5 result (thank-you signer "The rooftop runners")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The rooftop runners") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. Plural, breathless. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: You beat our lap record delivering them.

terms.what: Makers of paper lanterns for China's lantern festival. Voice of the thank-you: Aurelia – High Quality Realistic Princess.
where: UI: level 5-6 result (thank-you signer "The lantern makers")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The lantern makers") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. Plural, warm. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: A thousand lights, thanks to you.

terms.what: Monks of a Chinese mountain monastery near the Dragon's lair, who get mountain tea. Voice of the thank-you: Mossbeard | The God of the Wild.
where: UI: level 5-7 result (thank-you signer "The mountain monks")
terms.guidance: Signs the thank-you note on the level result ("— The mountain monks") and voices it. Translate as a natural description (not a name) and keep the cargo's recipient wording in step with it. Plural, calm and slow ("Sit. Rest."). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Sit. Rest. The last climb is steep.

terms.what: The Great Sphinx of Giza as a character: the recipient of new riddles (2-4) and of Neferhoo's 4,000-year-late letter; "too polite to complain". Its note closes last-2-6, read in its own voice (Matthew Schmitz – Ancient Sage Dragon Wizard), dry and slow.
where: story (before-2-4, last-2-6 and the note "Signed: the Sphinx.")
flight voice (birds greet it: "Hi, Mister Sphinx!")
terms.guidance: Use your language's usual name for the Sphinx (the monument), with the article/capital your language gives it. Peaches calls it "Mister Sphinx", so treat it as masculine. It signs its note itself: "Signed: the Sphinx." Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: “Delivered at last. Worth the wait. Signed: the Sphinx.”

terms.what: A curious robot in Cyberpunk City who receives a paper letter (5-4) and thanks the courier in robotic CAPITALS. Voice: Silent Systemus – Sovereign Protocol.
where: data: cargo 5-4 ("a curious robot"), thank-you signer 5-4
terms.guidance: A robot's serial name: translate "Unit" with the word your language uses for a machine's model/unit designation and keep the number 7 (or keep "Unit 7" if that reads as a robot name). Its thank-you is ALL CAPS, short and formal; keep that style. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: PAPER. MARVELLOUS. I SHALL FRAME IT.

terms.what: The Pirate Captain's parrot, his first mate; it never speaks. The Captain gives it orders ("Log it, Parrot!") and it stays at the club in the end ("The parrot stayed. He says hello.").
terms.guidance: Use your ordinary word for parrot; capitalised "Parrot" when the Captain addresses it as a name. Masculine ("He says hello"). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Every route? …Parrot, strike the colours. We be collectors now!

terms.what: Baron Bat's bats, whom he calls his cousins and relatives; they "never miss a party" and fly in as his vanguard and helpers.
where: flight voice (baron summon: "Cousins! We have company.")
terms.guidance: Bill's joke: the jungle bats are the Baron's family. Use the family words (cousins, relatives) naturally. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Bats. The Baron’s cousins never miss a party. Keep your beak up.

terms.what: Bill's title: head of the Sky Club post office.
terms.guidance: The local word for the head of a post office (postmaster / jefe de correos / Postmeister / chef de poste…); friendly, a little old-fashioned. Pip says "Postmaster's orders", so it also works alone. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Keep your beak up. Postmaster's orders. Beak... up.

terms.what: Baron Bat's epithet on his entrance name card (a storm of bats).
where: UI: boss name card (all caps, under the name)
terms.guidance: Grand, short, all caps; must fit the card under the name. "Storm" = his storm of bats and fireballs; pairs with title.the-storm-returns.

terms.what: Epithet of the upgraded Baron Bat when he comes back in endless flights (with the sonic screech); his arrival headline then reads "THE BARON RETURNS".
terms.guidance: Echo title.lord-of-the-storm's "storm" word. All caps, short.

terms.what: The Spitter King's epithet on his name card (he brews, and commands a swarm of beetles).
terms.guidance: All caps, short. "Brewer" ties to his brew (story.brew); "swarm" here means his beetles, not the Swarm rush path, so a different word is fine if more natural.

terms.what: The Dusk Empress's epithet on her name card; the "veil" is her silk shield (attack.veil).
terms.guidance: All caps, poetic, short. Use the same "veil" word as the fight hints ("FIRE WHEN THE VEIL DROPS").

terms.what: The Pirate Captain's epithet on his title ribbon.
terms.guidance: All caps, swashbuckling. "High tide" = hazard.tide's HIGH TIDE.

terms.what: The Ember Dragon's epithet on his name card.
terms.guidance: All caps, majestic, short enough for the card.

terms.what: Neferhoo's epithet on his guardian card (KEEPER OF THE LOST LETTER): he guarded the one lost letter for 4,000 years.
terms.guidance: Singular "the Lost Letter" (one specific letter). Keep it related to but distinct from title.keeper-of-lost-letters, the club job Bill offers him at the end (plural, all lost mail).

terms.what: The Sky Club job Bill offers Neferhoo after his fall: looking after all lost mail.
terms.guidance: Plural and general, a job title said aloud by Bill; Neferhoo answers "Lost letters? …". Echo the wording of his card epithet (title.keeper-of-the-lost-letter) so the payoff is felt. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Neferhoo, the club needs a Keeper of Lost Letters. Care to apply?

terms.what: Neferhoo's own proud title: courier of the Pharaoh's post.
where: flight voice (Pip: "Royal Courier? I'm just Courier. Courier Pip.")
terms.guidance: Use the SAME word for courier as char.courier: Pip's joke depends on it ("Royal Courier? I'm just Courier."). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Neferhoo, Royal Courier. Four thousand years on this route.

terms.what: Neferhoo's descriptive nickname in the docs and the "Return to Sender" achievement description: a courier who is a mummy.
terms.guidance: Mummy (wrapped Egyptian body) + courier (same word as char.courier). Not spoken; Pip and Peaches say "A mummy with a mailbag!"

terms.what: King Coo's epithet (COMMISSIONER OF THE CURB on his card): a police commissioner whose beat is the pavement edge where pigeons forage.
terms.guidance: Wordplay: the "curb" (kerb) is the street edge where pigeons peck for crumbs, and to "curb" is to restrain, police. Recreate a pompous street-police title, alliterative if possible; all caps, card-short.

terms.what: King Coo's rank (a police commissioner), which he uses to speak of himself in the third person; also the club job he takes ("Commissioner wanted").
terms.guidance: Police rank (chief of police). He refers to himself as "the Commissioner" (third person: "The Commissioner accepts."); the courier and Bill address him as "Commissioner". Keep the same word in all four uses. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: A bagel a day? …The Commissioner accepts.

terms.what: The Searchlight Gargoyle's epithet (WATCHMAN OF THE TALLEST TOWER on his card).
terms.guidance: All caps, card-short; alliteration (W-T-T) is a bonus. "The tallest tower" = place.tallest-tower.

terms.what: The club job the Spitter King accepts ("Royal ink-maker!"): he makes the club's ink, no boiling the post.
terms.guidance: Plain job noun; the King promotes himself to "Royal ink-maker", so keep the same base word. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Royal ink-maker! I shall need a bigger flask.

terms.what: Chapter 1's first stop (levels 1-1 to 1-3) and the endless tour's first region: a tropical rainforest canopy with toucans, sloths and roosting bats.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: The generic rainforest ("the jungle"), not a named country; a short map label. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Five somebodies. The nearest roosts in the jungle and calls himself a Baron.

terms.what: Chapter 1, levels 1-4 and 1-5: carnival week in Rio with samba macaws, confetti, Sugarloaf Mountain and a football gale.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard country name in your language. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Brazil! It’s carnival week, so half the mail is confetti.

terms.what: Chapter 1, levels 1-6 to 1-8 (Baron Bat's lair): a stepped Aztec temple at sunrise.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: A region named after the Aztec civilisation (pre-Columbian Mexico), used as a place label: use the natural noun/adjective form for "Aztec lands/temple" in your language, short.

terms.what: Chapter 2, levels 2-1 to 2-3: golden Ancient Rome with the Colosseum, chariots and statues.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: The historical city/empire, "Ancient" = antiquity; keep parallel with "Ancient Arabia".

terms.what: Chapter 2, levels 2-4 to 2-6 (Neferhoo): the Nile, the pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx at noon.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard country name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Egypt! We’ve delivered here for four thousand years and lost one letter.

terms.what: Chapter 2, levels 2-7 to 2-9 (the Spitter King's lair): a teal dawn over an ancient Arabian city with a lantern bazaar, caravans and flying carpets.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: A storybook "ancient Arabia" (Arabian Nights mood), not a modern country; parallel in form to "Ancient Rome". Arabic translators: use a neutral historical form.

terms.what: Chapter 3, levels 3-1 to 3-4 (King Coo and the Searchlight Gargoyle): a rainy New York night with skyscrapers, a theatre marquee, newsstands, cabs and steam vents.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard city name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: New York, and not one lamp lit. The night mail can’t find a single door.

terms.what: Chapter 3, levels 3-5 to 3-8 (the Dusk Empress's lair): the City of Light at night, rooftop painters, an accordion, crystal rooftops. Locked "Coming soon" in this build.

terms.guidance: Standard city name; its epithet "the City of Light" is place.city-of-light. The map ribbon reads "Paris — coming soon". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: To be continued… Next stop: Paris, the City of Light.

terms.what: Chapter 4, levels 4-1 to 4-3: a Mexican coast at dusk with two volcanoes, marigolds, papel picado and a harbour. Locked in this build.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard country name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Marigolds everywhere! Mexico knows what a hummingbird likes.

terms.what: Chapter 4, levels 4-4 to 4-8 (the Pirate Captain's lair): open water at dawn, ferries, whales, gulls; "nowhere to land, and the sea bites". Locked in this build.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: The high seas, far from land; short label.

terms.what: Chapter 5, levels 5-1 and 5-2: polar twilight with auroras, a penguin choir and a polar station. Locked in this build.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard continent name.

terms.what: Chapter 5, levels 5-3 to 5-5: a neon cyberpunk megacity where everything is sent by wire; noodle bars, robots. Locked in this build.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: A fictional city named after the genre: keep "cyberpunk" as the usual loanword (or your genre term) + city; short map label.

terms.what: Chapter 5, levels 5-6 to 5-8 (the Ember Dragon's lair): a red sun over stacked mountains, sky lanterns and a monastery, at the far end of the map. Locked in this build.
where: UI: level card and its accessibility label
terms.guidance: Standard country name.

terms.what: Bill's and the narrator's epithet for Paris ("Paris, the City of Light. Or it was, until last night.").
where: story (before-3-5-0, last-3-4-6 "To be continued… Next stop: Paris, the City of Light.")
terms.guidance: Use your language's established epithet for Paris (fr "la Ville Lumière"); the joke is that its lights went out. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Paris, the City of Light. Or it was, until last night.

terms.what: Where the Ember Dragon lives, past the end of every route; the address on his letter ("The Ember Dragon, Edge of the Map") and the new route six he lights.
where: flight voice (dragon: "It is quiet at the edge of the map.")
terms.guidance: Use EXACTLY the same words as chapter 5 (chapter.edge-of-the-map) and the achievement; capitalised when it is a name or address, lowercase in running speech ("at the edge of the map"). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The edge of the map. No route has ever run past here.

terms.what: The Egyptian site of the pyramids and the Sphinx; part of the address on Neferhoo's lost letter ("To the Sphinx, Giza.").
terms.guidance: Standard exonym for Giza; it is written like a postal address line. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: “To the Sphinx, Giza.” …It was right outside the whole time.

terms.what: The river of Egypt; level 2-4 is "Nile Switchbacks".
terms.guidance: Standard name of the river. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The Nile is sparkling! Hello, boats! Hello, palm trees!

terms.what: The Great Pyramid in Egypt, where Neferhoo was sealed with his last letter; "The pyramid's dust is stirring…" announces him.
where: UI: Neferhoo arrival banner ("THE PYRAMID STIRS")
terms.guidance: Plain word for pyramid; keep the same word in the banner, the NPC names and the voice lines. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The pyramid’s dust is stirring…

terms.what: The Roman amphitheatre, mentioned in the birds' Rome small talk.
terms.guidance: Standard name of the monument. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The Colosseum! Fifty thousand seats. I'd be too nervous to watch.

terms.what: Rio de Janeiro's landmark peak (Pão de Açúcar); Pip jokes it is "not actually made of sugar".
terms.guidance: Use the established local name (pt-BR "Pão de Açúcar"); keep Pip's sugar joke if the local name also means sugar, otherwise adapt the line. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Sugarloaf Mountain! Not actually made of sugar. I checked.

terms.what: The Paris landmark, in Peaches's Paris small talk.
terms.guidance: Standard name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Bonjour, Paris! The Eiffel Tower is twinkling just for us!

terms.what: The illuminated canopy over a New York theatre entrance (cargo 3-1 needs its light bulbs); King Coo's missing bread cart was sheltering under it all night.
terms.guidance: The lit sign/canopy over a theatre's door (not a tent). Keep the same word in the cargo and in the story payoff. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The marquee? It was under the marquee. Out of the rain. All night.

terms.what: New York's tallest skyscraper, where the Searchlight Gargoyle sits on a ledge and whose weather vane the courier delivers.
terms.guidance: Same words as the cargo ("for the tallest tower") and the Gargoyle's epithet; "the tower keeper" (npc.tower-keeper) keeps it. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: A weather vane for the tallest tower. It keeps spinning. Me too.

terms.what: The jungle treetops: the Canopy Route's territory, which Baron Bat claimed ("The canopy is yours. Take it.").
where: Play Games achievements "Mail Through the Canopy", "Gold Canopy"
terms.guidance: Forest canopy (the roof of leaves), the same word as in chapter.canopy-route. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Tell you what, Baron. From now on, we deliver the canopy at dusk.

terms.what: The lantern bazaar of Ancient Arabia (level 2-7 "Lantern Bazaar").
terms.guidance: Standard word for an oriental market. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The bazaar at dawn. You can smell the King’s brew from here.

terms.what: The harbours of the Tide Route, whose bells ring when the post comes in.
terms.guidance: Plain word for a port/harbour; British spelling in the source. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The tide route. Harbour bells ring when the post comes in. None has rung all week.

terms.what: Chapter 1 (Jungle, Brazil, Aztec; boss Baron Bat): the mail route through the jungle treetops.
where: UI: campaign map banner ("CHAPTER N · THE CANOPY ROUTE")
UI: postcard ("— The Canopy Route", "Postcard from …")
terms.guidance: A mail route over the forest canopy. "Route" is the key recurring word for the Sky Club's mail routes: use the same word as story.mail-route. Shown in caps on the map banner; keep it short.

terms.what: Chapter 2 (Ancient Rome, Egypt, Ancient Arabia; boss the Spitter King, guardian Neferhoo): "Rome to the desert bazaars. The oldest route on the map."
where: UI: campaign map banner ("CHAPTER N · THE ANCIENT ROAD")
UI: postcard ("— The Ancient Road", "Postcard from …")
terms.guidance: An old trade road through antiquity; the Spitter King calls it "my road" ("Every letter on my road goes in the brew!"), so keep the same noun. Shown in caps on the map banner; keep it short. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The ancient road: Rome to the desert bazaars. The oldest route on the map.

terms.what: Chapter 3 (New York, Paris; boss the Dusk Empress, guardians King Coo and the Searchlight Gargoyle): the city route of lamps and night mail.
where: UI: campaign map banner ("CHAPTER N · THE LAMPLIGHT LINE")
UI: postcard ("— The Lamplight Line", "Postcard from …")
terms.guidance: "Line" as in a transport/delivery line; L-L alliteration. The theme is lamps going dark (the Empress) and light (the Gargoyle's searchlight); keep the lamp image. Shown in caps on the map banner; keep it short.

terms.what: Chapter 4 (Mexico, Open Sea; boss the Pirate Captain): the sea route ruled by the tide.
where: UI: campaign map banner ("CHAPTER N · THE TIDE ROUTE")
UI: postcard ("— The Tide Route", "Postcard from …")
terms.guidance: A mail route by sea; "tide" = hazard.tide. Bill says "The tide route." aloud. Shown in caps on the map banner; keep it short. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The tide route. Harbour bells ring when the post comes in. None has rung all week.

terms.what: Chapter 5 (Antarctica, Cyberpunk City, China; boss the Ember Dragon): the far end of the world, where no route has ever run.
where: UI: campaign map banner ("CHAPTER N · THE EDGE OF THE MAP")
UI: postcard ("— The Edge of the Map", "Postcard from …")
terms.guidance: Same words as place.edge-of-the-map and the achievement "Edge of the Map". Shown in caps on the map banner; keep it short. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Three seals now. And every one posted from the edge of the map.

terms.what: Campaign level 1-1 (Jungle). The courier's very first job (30 s, tap to flap). Its intro card hint: "Tap to flap. Fly through the stars."
where: UI: Records / saved sessions (a campaign flight is named after its level)
terms.guidance: Plain and warm: "the first delivery". Title case, short: it sits on a map node label and the level card. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Hold still, little birthday card. The toucan twins are waiting. First delivery...

terms.what: Campaign level 1-2 (Jungle). Teaches chaining stars into a streak for the 3× multiplier. Its intro card hint: "Chain stars for 3×; three perfect gates earn a magnet."
where: UI: Records / saved sessions (a campaign flight is named after its level)
terms.guidance: Use the same "streak" word as ui.streak; alliteration is a bonus. Title case, short: it sits on a map node label and the level card.

terms.what: Campaign level 1-3 (Jungle). First bats to shoot. Its intro card hint: "Shoot. Tap Shoot to knock out bats."
where: UI: Records / saved sessions (a campaign flight is named after its level)
terms.guidance: A patrol of bats (bats on patrol). Short. Title case, short: it sits on a map node label and the level card.

terms.what: Campaign level 1-4 (Brazil). Brazil's carnival, with the first gale (it blows footballs). Its intro card hint: "Gale! Watch the ! and dodge the footballs."
where: UI: Records / saved sessions (a campaign flight is named after its level)
terms.guidance: Carnival + skies; festive. Title case, short: it sits on a map node label and the level card.

terms.what: Campaign level 1-5 (Brazil). Introduces Sprint. Its intro card hint: "Sprint smashes bats and surges ahead."
where: UI: Records / saved sessions (a campaign flight is named after its level)
terms.guidance: Express mail service. Use the SAME phrase as attack.express-post (Neferhoo's fury attack "EXPRESS POST"). Title case, short: it sits on a map node label and the level card. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Enough! EXPRESS POST!

flight voice (neferhoo summon "Catch, fledgling! It always comes back.")
terms.guidance: Use the standard name of the Egyptian symbol (ankh / anj / Anch / アンク…). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Shoot his letters back, rookie. And mind the ankh: it comes back!

terms.what: Neferhoo's fury: five letters, faster ("FURY · Express post and two ankhs"); he shouts "Enough! EXPRESS POST!".
terms.guidance: Same words as level 1-5 "Express Post" (level.1-5): express mail. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Enough! EXPRESS POST!

terms.what: The basic obstacle: a wall with an opening (gap) the bird flies through; a "perfect gate/pass" goes through dead centre. Also "passage" in docs, "gap"/"opening" in lines.
where: UI: everywhere (results "total gates", daily goal "Clear N gates", builder "Gate")
flight voice ("Three perfect gates, one magnet!")
terms.guidance: One word for the obstacle the bird passes through, used in the HUD, goals, upgrades ("Perfect gates needed") and builder. "gap" and "opening" are its hole. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Three perfect gates, one magnet! Stars, come to Pip!

terms.what: The plain, still gate family that opens every level (and can hold a stone door).
terms.guidance: A garden gate (hedge/fence gate). Builder label.
terms.example: Only a garden gate can hold a stone door.

terms.what: A gate family whose opening rises and falls on the wind.
terms.guidance: An updraft that lifts the opening. Builder label.

terms.what: A gate family of flower-petal shutters whose opening narrows and widens; Bill calls them "petal gates" that "open and shut to the music".
terms.guidance: Shutters made of petals. Bill's "petal gates" is the same obstacle: keep the petal word in both. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: And mind the petal gates. They open and shut to the music.

terms.what: A gate family with two openings that slide apart ("up one gap, down the next"); level 2-4 is "Nile Switchbacks".
terms.guidance: Like a zigzag mountain road: up one gap, down the next. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: The Sphinx won’t say. Mind the switchbacks: up one gap, down the next.

terms.what: A floating gate family of hanging lanterns that bob.
terms.guidance: Builder label.

terms.what: A floating gate family of wheels that close in and back (New York and later).
terms.guidance: Builder label.

terms.what: A gate family of crystal steps in a ripple, three at a time (Paris rooftops).
where: story (before-3-5-2 "Steps of it, three at a time.")
terms.guidance: Builder label; same crystal word as level 3-5.

terms.what: A breakable stone slab that seals a gate's opening (from 2-2); break it with a charged rock or Sprint. The builder calls it "Stone door".
where: data: hint 2-2 ("Hold Shoot for a big rock that breaks stone.")
UI: Sprint label ("Rush ahead to smash bats and stone panels")
terms.guidance: Same stone word in panel/door/wall; the birds joke about it ("Stone wall? More like stone suggestion."). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Crumble! Stone panel, meet physics!

terms.what: New York's steam geysers (3-3, 3-4): vents in the street that hiss, then burst; hop over the hot ones, ride the soft ones.
terms.guidance: A street steam vent/geyser. "hot" vents hurt, "soft" ones carry the bird up: keep the hot/soft and hop/ride pairs short. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Vents hiss, then burst. Hop the hot ones, ride the soft ones.

terms.what: The water across the bottom of the screen in the Pirate Captain's fight and the sea levels; touching it hurts ("Splash!").
where: UI: caption "STAY OUT OF THE WATER"
terms.guidance: "the sea" and "the water" are the same hazard; Bill: "the sea bites". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Open water. Nowhere to land, and the sea bites.

terms.what: The Pirate Captain's rising sea: a bell rings, then the tide surges up ("TIDE RISING · Fly high!", "HIGH TIDE · Stay above the water").
where: UI: fight tags, HIGH TIDE label
data: hint 4-5 ("When the bell rings, fly high.")
terms.guidance: Tide / high tide. Same word as chapter.tide-route and title.terror-of-the-high-tide. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: High tide, feathers! Fly or swim!

terms.what: The harbour bell that rings before each tide surge.
where: flight voice (tide-bell: "Bell rings, we fly high!")
terms.guidance: A ship/harbour bell; ties to story.harbour-bells. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: When the bell rings, fly high.

terms.what: The lava that blasts up from below in the Eruption rush; hop over the plumes.
where: data: hint 4-2 ("Hop over the lava plumes.")
terms.guidance: A jet of lava from the ground. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Hop over the lava plumes.

terms.what: Space rocks that fall in the Skyfall rush; ring sprints smash them. Also the duel prize "Meteor shower".
terms.guidance: Shooting stars / space rocks. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Ring sprints smash meteors.

terms.what: What a gale blows across the sky (junk; over Brazil, footballs); dodge where the "!" flashes.
where: UI: gale banner ("Dodge the debris where the ! flashes!")
UI: replay highlight ("Dodged the flying debris.")
terms.guidance: Flying junk. Keep it short. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Dodge the debris where the ! flashes!

terms.what: Over Brazil, the gale's debris are footballs (soccer balls), a different ball each gust.
where: data: hint 1-4 ("Gale! Watch the ! and dodge the footballs.")
terms.guidance: Soccer ball (association football), the natural word in your market (pt-BR "bolas de futebol").
terms.example: Gale! Watch the ! and dodge the footballs.

terms.what: The flashing exclamation-mark warnings of a gale that show where debris will fly ("Watch the !").
terms.guidance: The "!" symbol itself stays as is (it is a sign drawn in the sky); translate the sentence around it ("Watch the !") naturally.
terms.example: Gale! Watch the ! and take the open side.

terms.what: The rubble barriers of a rush path, whose openings trace the route; Sprint and ring sprints smash them.
terms.guidance: Broken stone and debris.

terms.what: A rush path: a short scripted run of six beats of stars and gold sprint rings with danger from one side (Wildfire, Skyfall, Eruption or Swarm); a big banner names it, escaping it scores a bonus ("ESCAPED! +N", "FLAWLESS! +N").
where: data: hint 5-1 ("Any rush can come now. Read the banner!")
terms.guidance: A rush = a sudden dash/stampede. Keep the word short (HUD "RUSH ×2!"). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Any rush can come now. Read the banner!

terms.what: The rush path where fire chases from behind; outrun it through the gold rings ("WILDFIRE!", "Outran the wildfire"). Level 2-3 is "Wildfire Run".
where: UI: escape banner and replay highlight
data: hint 2-3 ("Fly through the gold rings to outrun the fire!")
terms.guidance: A forest/bush fire. Banner word in caps with "!": short. Same word in the level name 2-3. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Wildfire! The rings outrun it! Go!

terms.what: The rush path where meteors fall from above; ring sprints smash them ("SKYFALL!", "Survived the skyfall"). Level 2-5 is "Skyfall".
where: UI: escape banner and replay highlight
terms.guidance: A coined word: the sky falling (meteors). Make a short, punchy word or phrase meaning "falling sky / meteor fall"; the same word is level 2-5's name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Skyfall! Sprint the rings, quick!

terms.what: The rush path where lava blasts up from below; hop over the plumes ("ERUPTION!", "Beat the eruption").
terms.guidance: Volcanic eruption. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Eruption! Hop over the plumes!

terms.what: The rush path where a swarm of bats streams in from ahead; sprint through them ("SWARM!", "Plowed through the swarm"). Also the Dragon's bat flocks ("SWARM · Dodge the bats or sprint through them").
terms.guidance: A swarm (of bats). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Bats! Hundreds! Sprint through!

terms.what: A storm wind that blows the bird along with a tailwind while debris flies; watch the "!" and take the open side ("GALE!", "WEATHERED", "You rode out the gale"). Endless gales grow fiercer each time.
terms.guidance: A strong storm wind. Same word in level 3-6's name and the banner. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Gale! Warning sign says: open side!

terms.what: The end of a campaign or built level: a candy-striped gate with a FINISH sign, flags/pennants and a checkered tape the bird bursts; reaching it completes the level.
where: UI: level card ("Reach the finish", "About N s to the finish")
terms.guidance: Race finish line; "FINISH" on the sign is a short all-caps word. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Finish line! Gold pennants spotted! Exactly as described!

terms.what: The 30-second flight before a boss or guardian arrives on a boss level ("A 30 s run-up first").
terms.guidance: The approach before the fight.

terms.what: The three waves of small enemies a boss sends before arriving (Baron Bat, Spitter King, Dusk Empress, King Coo); a banner names them ("BARON BAT'S BATS") and a plate counts them down ("N LEFT", "CLEAR!").
where: UI: captions ("Here they come! The Baron is right behind.")
terms.guidance: The word "vanguard" itself is not shown; the banner shows the group's name.
terms.example: Here they come! The Baron is right behind.

terms.what: The main collectible: stars on the route, three per passage. Collecting them scores, builds the streak, restores the shield, rates the level (★★/★★★ marks) and fills the star wallet for upgrades and birds. "Star points" is the endless score.
where: UI: everywhere (HUD, level card, results, wallet "stars to spend", map total "12 / 63")
terms.guidance: ONE word for star in all its uses (pickup, rating, wallet currency); the rating stars are the same stars. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Tap to flap. Fly through the stars.

terms.what: A group of three stars; collecting all three pays a +5 bonus ("STAR TRIO +5!"); replay highlights call the first one a constellation.
terms.guidance: Three stars as a set; short.
terms.example: Three stars become a constellation. +5 points!

terms.what: A life: a flight starts with three hearts and a shield; losing the last heart ends it. Bosses knock hearts loose as they grow stronger ("HEART ×2"); the builder places hearts.
terms.guidance: The life-heart icon word. Peaches plays on hearts as love; keep "heart". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: One heart left. One is still a whole number!

terms.what: The bubble around the bird that absorbs one hit; collected stars refill it (every ninth star at the start). Also an upgrade and a duel prize.
terms.guidance: Birds also call it "bubble": use one shield word in UI and voice. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Phew! Shield absorbed one hundred percent!

terms.what: A temporary power earned by flying through perfect gates (three in the campaign at first): it pulls nearby stars to the bird for some seconds ("STAR MAGNET!").
where: data: hint 1-2 ("three perfect gates earn a magnet")
terms.guidance: Magnet that attracts stars; the upgrade card shortens it to "Magnet". Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Magnet on! Eight seconds! Seven! Six! Ooh, shiny!

terms.what: The gold rings of a rush path: flying through one starts a ring sprint; catching all six gives a bonus sprint ("SPRINT RING!", "ALL RINGS!"). Hints and voices call them "the gold rings".
where: UI: HUD pop-up, rush banner ("Grab the sprint rings and outrun it!")
data: hint 2-3 ("Fly through the gold rings")
terms.guidance: "sprint ring", "gold rings" and "the rings" are the same object: keep one ring word. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Fly through the gold rings to outrun the fire!

terms.what: Floating boxes in the 1 v 1 duel; a bird opens one by flying into it or shooting it, and gets an attack sent at its rival (Bat swarm, Spitter beetle, Meteor shower) or a help (Heart, Shield, Star power).
where: UI: duel setup and HUD ("Grab the mystery boxes!")
terms.guidance: A surprise/lucky box.
terms.example: Grab the mystery boxes!

terms.what: Duel mystery-box attack: a line of swarm bats streams in at the rival's height.
terms.guidance: Short label; same bat/swarm words as set-piece.swarm.

terms.what: Duel mystery-box attack: meteors fall where the rival is flying.
terms.guidance: Short label; same meteor word as hazard.meteor.

terms.what: Duel mystery-box help: for a few seconds nothing hurts the bird, it smashes what it touches and hurts its rival on contact.
terms.guidance: Invincibility power; short label. (Peaches's "Star power!" streak line uses the same words loosely.)

terms.what: Upgrade: how far Shoot can charge a bigger, harder rock (Max charge).
terms.guidance: Upgrade card title; short.
terms.example: Hold Shoot to charge a bigger, harder rock.

terms.what: Upgrade: Sprint's burst length and cooldown ("A speed burst that smashes enemies in your way.").
terms.guidance: Same word as weapon.sprint.
terms.example: A speed burst that smashes enemies in your way.

terms.what: Upgrade: how many stars refill the shield and the safe time after it breaks.
terms.guidance: Same word as pickup.shield.
terms.example: Blocks one hit for you. Collect stars in flight to refill it.

terms.what: Upgrade: perfect gates needed, how long the star magnet lasts and its reach.
terms.guidance: Same word as pickup.star-magnet.
terms.example: Fly perfectly through gates to earn it. It pulls stars to you.

terms.what: The fire button (on from 1-1): a tap throws a rock; holding it charges a bigger rock. Also the verb in hints ("Shoot the seeds down").
where: UI: flight button and its label
terms.guidance: Button label: one short imperative/noun, the SAME word in the button, the hints ("Tap Shoot", "Hold Shoot") and Bill's tips. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Shoot. Tap Shoot to knock out bats.

terms.what: The bird's ammunition: small rocks thrown with Shoot ("Rock beats shot!"). "Rocks" are counted: "Out of rocks".
where: story (before-1-6 "Then we knock politely. With rocks.")
UI: "Hold to charge a bigger rock"
terms.guidance: Pebble/stone thrown by the bird; the Dragon calls one a "pebble". Keep the rock word for the jokes ("Sticks and stones? I brought the stones!"). Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Then we knock politely. With rocks.

terms.what: A charged shot: hold Shoot to charge a bigger, harder rock that breaks stone and shatters enemy shots.
where: data: hint 2-2 ("Hold Shoot for a big rock that breaks stone.")
UI: upgrades ("Hold Shoot to charge a bigger, harder rock.")
UI: Shoot button state ("Charging N%", "Full charge")
terms.guidance: Charged / bigger rock; same rock word.
terms.example: Hold Shoot for a big rock that breaks stone.

terms.what: The rock reserve: every shot spends from it and it refills after a pause ("Ammo N%", "Reloading…").
terms.guidance: Short. The birds never say "ammo", they say "rocks".

terms.what: The burst button (from 1-5): a short surge of speed that smashes bats and stone panels in the way, then recharges ("SMASH!"). Off on 3-4.
where: UI: flight button and its states ("Ready", "Sprinting", "Recharging, N seconds")
terms.guidance: Button label: one short word, the same in the button, the hints ("No Sprint here.") and upgrades. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Sprint smashes bats and surges ahead.

terms.what: The 2-second boost a sprint ring gives (3× speed); it smashes meteors and outruns fire and lava.
terms.guidance: Sprint word + ring word, as in pickup.sprint-ring. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Ring sprints smash meteors.

terms.what: The pop-up when Sprint or star power rams an enemy or a panel ("SMASH!", "SMASH +N!").
terms.guidance: Comic impact word, all caps, short.
terms.example: Tap the sky to flap. Hold Shoot to charge. Sprint to smash!

terms.what: The story mode: one trip around the world over 5 routes, 13 regions and 41 levels, each a delivery, with story scenes, bosses and guardians. Tap & Fly only.
terms.guidance: Standard game word for a story campaign. Home key label in caps: short.

terms.what: The high-score mode: one endless Tap & Fly flight that tours the world's regions and meets the bosses in turn, with three hearts and a shield ("Fly as far as you can").
where: UI: home key ("ENDLESS", "Fly as far as you can")
terms.guidance: Use the usual word for an endless/infinite mode; also used as an adjective ("endless flight", "endless sky").
terms.example: Endless. Fly as far as you can.

terms.what: The main touch control: tap to flap. Every campaign, endless, co-op and duel flight is Tap & Fly; in the builder it is one of the four level kinds.
terms.guidance: A mode name built on the verbs tap + fly; keep the "&" pattern shared with "Squat & Fly" and "Jump & Fly" if your language allows.
terms.example: Endless · Tap & Fly

terms.what: Camera mini game: the player's push-ups move the bird (lower to dip, push up to soar).
terms.guidance: A side mini game, not the core of the game. Use your fitness word for push-up.

terms.what: Camera mini game: squats move the bird (squat to descend, stand to rise).
terms.guidance: Same pattern as Tap & Fly.

terms.what: Camera mini game: jumps give the bird a big boost, then it glides.
terms.guidance: Same pattern as Tap & Fly.

terms.what: The side menu of camera games (Push-Up Flight, Squat & Fly, Jump & Fly) and two-player Fly Together ("Move to fly, or share the phone with a friend.").
terms.guidance: Beakbound is a tap-to-fly adventure; these are side games. Avoid wording that makes the app sound like a fitness app.
terms.example: Move to fly, or share the phone with a friend.

terms.what: Two players on one phone (left and right halves): Roped co-op, No rope, or the 1 v 1 duel ("TWO PLAYERS · ONE PHONE").
terms.guidance: Mode title; friendly, short.

terms.what: Fly Together co-op where the two birds share one rope: flap together to climb; a bird flapping alone lifts both a little; Sprint drags the partner.
where: UI: co-op mode picker ("Roped: the birds share a rope")
Play Games achievement "Two on One Phone"
terms.guidance: Tied together with a rope; short label.
terms.example: Roped: the birds share a rope

terms.what: Fly Together co-op without the rope: each bird flies on its own; hearts, shield and score are shared.
terms.guidance: Short label, the opposite of Roped.
terms.example: No rope: each bird flies on its own

terms.what: Fly Together duel: the two birds fight each other with their own hearts and mystery boxes; last bird flying wins ("Ready to duel…", "Player 1 wins!").
where: UI: co-op mode picker ("1 v 1: the birds fight each other")
terms.guidance: Keep the numeric "1 v 1" form if your language uses it ("1 contre 1", "1 gegen 1", "1 對 1"…); the noun is "duel".
terms.example: 1 v 1: the birds fight each other

terms.what: The editor where players place gates, stars, hearts, enemies and the finish by hand, test fly and share levels by code; opens after five scored flights.
where: UI: home key ("LEVEL BUILDER", "Make · fly · share")
terms.guidance: Mode title; short (home key in caps).
terms.example: Level Builder. Make your own levels, fly them and share them.

terms.what: The daily Adventure: three rotating goals a day on a themed postcard ("Today's little adventure."); finishing all three stamps the card. The only place flight goals live.
where: UI: home key ("Adventure", "Today’s adventure. N of 3 goals complete.")
terms.guidance: Use an inviting word for a small daily adventure; keep it short on the home key.
terms.example: Today’s little adventure.

terms.what: The practice/test flights where nothing is scored (docs name; the UI shows "Practice" and "Test flight").
terms.guidance: Mostly a docs term; if shown, translate like a flying school. Replays and Flight School stay silent (no flight voices).

terms.what: A flight that is not scored or saved as a record (builder test flights, practice).
terms.guidance: Short tag.

terms.what: In the Level Builder, flying your own level to try it ("TEST FLY", "Test flight · nothing is saved"); a test flight that reaches the finish marks the level "cleared by its maker".
terms.guidance: Use your aviation word for a test flight; "test fly" is the verb.
terms.example: Test flight: Up and Down steer.

terms.what: The legacy course (one chance, count the gates) kept so old sessions still load.
terms.guidance: Rarely seen; a plain "classic" label.
terms.example: Classic: fly through the gaps.

terms.what: Endless flights tour all 13 regions in turn, each with its own sky; the birds comment on each new region.
where: UI: postcard 5 ("The endless sky is still out there")
terms.guidance: Docs term.

terms.what: The bird club that runs the post: the courier's employer and family. Its rule is "Every letter lands."; beaten bosses join it.
where: story (passim: "Welcome to the Sky Club post.", "the club needs…")
flight voice ("Fastest escape in Sky Club history!")
terms.guidance: An in-world organisation: translate the descriptive name once (sky + club) and reuse it verbatim; "the club" is its short form. Bill's "Welcome to the club, Stoneface" is both literal and the idiom. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: There you are, rookie! Postmaster Bill. Welcome to the Sky Club post.

terms.what: The Sky Club's mail service, and the courier's greeting at every door ("Sky Club post!"); the prologue's place caption.
where: flight voice (Pip: "Sky Club post, taking off!")
UI: postcard stamp ("SKY CLUB POST", address line "Sky Club post")
terms.guidance: "post" = the postal service (not a pole, not a job post). As a greeting it works like a postman's announcement at the door ("Post!", "Correo!"). Keep the same phrase in captions, voice and the postcard stamp. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Sky Club post! I have a letter for you, sir.

terms.what: The Sky Passport: 8 stamps, each with bronze, silver and gold medals for long-term goals ("Your sky passport.", "Small adventures. Lasting souvenirs.").
terms.guidance: Travel passport; screen title. "Sky Passport" in docs.
terms.example: Your sky passport.

terms.what: One of the 8 passport goals (Frequent flyer, On the dot…), shown like a passport stamp/visa ink stamp; also the daily postcard is "stamped" when done ("POSTCARD STAMPED!").
where: UI: daily adventure ("Finish all three to stamp this card.")
terms.guidance: WARNING: the passport's "stamp" is an ink stamp (rubber stamp / visa stamp). The Pirate Captain's "stamps" are POSTAGE stamps (story.postage-stamp). Many languages use two different words (fr tampon vs timbre, de Stempel vs Briefmarke, ja スタンプ vs 切手): do not mix them.
terms.example: Finish all three to stamp this card.

terms.what: Each passport stamp has three medals won in order: Bronze, Silver, Gold (24 in all).
where: UI: passport, results, home key ("Passport. N of 24 medals.")
terms.guidance: Sports medal.
terms.example: No medal yet

terms.what: The first medal tier of a passport stamp.
terms.guidance: Medal metal; short label.
terms.example: Small adventures. Lasting souvenirs. Bronze, silver and gold for every stamp.

terms.what: The second medal tier.
terms.guidance: Medal metal; short label.
terms.example: Small adventures. Lasting souvenirs. Bronze, silver and gold for every stamp.

terms.what: The third (top) medal tier; also the "gold" of gold rings and the gold sets of achievements.
where: Play Games achievement names ("Gold Canopy", "Gold Road")
terms.guidance: Medal metal; same word in "Gold Canopy"/"Gold Road".
terms.example: Small adventures. Lasting souvenirs. Bronze, silver and gold for every stamp.

terms.what: A level's two star targets: collect the first mark for ★★, the second for ★★★ (★ for reaching the finish or beating the boss). Shown as notches on the in-flight star track; a chime when each lights.
where: UI: level card ("Collect N stars"), HUD track, results ("Both marks reached")
terms.guidance: A "mark" is a target line/notch. Pip punning "Top notch lit! Literally top notch!" needs adapting. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Second star locked in! One more notch to go!

terms.what: A finished level earns 1 to 3 stars ("2 of 3 stars", "Two stars", "Three stars"); the map shows them on each node and a total ("12 / 63").
where: UI: map node, level card, result, map total ("N of M campaign stars")
terms.guidance: Same star word as pickup.star.

terms.what: Stars collected in a row without missing one; it raises the multiplier (6 → 2×, 12 → 3×). "best streak" on results; passport stamp Constellation measures it.
where: UI: daily goal ("Collect N stars in one unbroken streak.")
terms.guidance: A run/chain of stars; same word as level 1-2's name. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Chain's growing! Don't miss one, don't miss one...

terms.what: The streak's score multiplier, 2× then 3× ("Chain stars for 3×").
terms.guidance: Score multiplier; keep the "×" sign. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Multiplier up! I love arithmetic when it sparkles!

terms.what: Flying through a gate right on its aiming mark ("PERFECT!"); perfect gates earn the star magnet and count for the On the dot stamp.
where: UI: passport ("Fly N perfect passes along the aiming marks.")
terms.guidance: "perfect pass" and "perfect gate" are the same achievement in flight. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: Three perfect gates, one magnet! Stars, come to Pip!

terms.what: The centre target in a gate's opening that a perfect pass flies through.
where: UI: replay highlights ("Right through the aiming mark.")
terms.guidance: A target/aim marker.
terms.example: Right through the aiming mark.

terms.what: Points in a flight; in endless the score is "star points" ("Score N points in one endless flight").
terms.guidance: Plain game word.

terms.what: A personal best score/stars ("NEW BEST!", "PERSONAL BEST", "Best: N stars", "Set your first best").
where: UI: home, results, level card, Level Builder
terms.guidance: Short; "record" is a separate word (ui.record).
terms.example: Set your first best

terms.what: A new endless high score ("New record!", "One more for a record"); Records is also the screen of saved flights.
where: flight voice (record: "New personal best! Can we frame the scoreboard?")
terms.guidance: High score record. Spoken in voice lines: captions, UI and voice must use the same wording.
terms.example: A record! Highest number we've EVER made!

terms.what: The screen with bests, campaign stars, workout totals, recent flights and saved sessions ("Your little victories.").
terms.guidance: Screen title; short.
terms.example: Your little victories.

terms.what: A flight the player chose to save, with its camera clip and replay ("Save session", "Saved sessions").
terms.guidance: Short.
terms.example: Could not save the session. Tap Save session to retry.

terms.what: Watching a saved flight again, reconstructed from its inputs ("Watch replay", "REPLAY").
terms.guidance: Video replay.
terms.example: The camera video and replay will be removed. Your scores stay in Records.

terms.what: The shop where stars buy upgrade levels for Shot power, Sprint, Shield and Magnet ("Power up your bird.", "Maxed").

terms.what: The star wallet: stars collected on scored flights that buy upgrades and birds ("YOUR STARS", "N stars to spend").
terms.guidance: Same star word as pickup.star (the currency IS the collected stars).

terms.what: The bird collection screen ("Meet your flight crew."): the four birds, their trails, unlock prices and the equipped one ("YOUR CO-PILOT", "Flying with you", "Fly with Pip").
